clue.text: Mood sours in the queues: such long journeys to the supermarket

definitions.text: such long journeys to the supermarket
definitions.note: plural phrase, matching a plural answer

indicators.note: the shuffled mood sits in the queues, so those letters go inside

parts.note: files are lines of people, i.e. queues

indicators.note: to sour is to go off or spoil, so the letters of the word mood turn bad and rearrange

explanation.surface: A grumble that a bad mood spreads through the shoppers waiting in line at the checkout.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase measures the distance produce travels from farm to shop, the long journeys behind supermarket shelves.

clue.text: Fine summer? Put in one more particular

indicators.note: the letter for one is put inside the other pieces

parts.note: a summer is one who sums, i.e. an adder
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Asks whether a fine summer could be made still more pleasant by adding one.
explanation.walkthrough: Summer reads as the season; it is someone who adds numbers up.
explanation.definitionFit: Faddy means fussy about food or habits, so the comparative means fussier.

clue.text: Chomping on cigar, concerned with carbon compounds

indicators.note: chomping chews things up, so the letters of on and cigar are mashed into a new order

explanation.surface: A smoker chewing a cigar, with a nod to the chemistry of tobacco.
explanation.definitionFit: Organic chemistry is the branch that studies compounds containing carbon.

clue.text: Computer game is the pits, one cries

parts.note: mines are pits dug for coal or ore
a weeper is one who cries

explanation.surface: A gamer moans that a computer game is dreadful and someone is in tears.
explanation.walkthrough: The pits looks like slang for awful; it means mines.
explanation.definitionFit: Minesweeper is the classic Windows puzzle game of clearing a grid without hitting hidden mines.

clue.text: Using no force is perfect for criminal

indicators.note: using no force means the word goes without the abbreviation for force

parts.note: flawless means perfect

explanation.surface: A claim that non-violence is ideal for a lawbreaker.
explanation.definitionFit: Lawless describes acting in defiance of the law, so it is an adjective for criminal behaviour.

clue.text: Bag half of goals at Chelsea

indicators.note: the answer is seven of the fourteen letters of the phrase goals at Chelsea, running on inside it

parts.note: the letters run across letters 5-11 of 'goals at Chelsea', the middle seven of fourteen

explanation.surface: A striker scores half of the goals at Chelsea football club.
explanation.walkthrough: Bag looks like a verb for scoring; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A satchel is a shoulder bag, traditionally carried by schoolchildren.

clue.text: Puts in the box or on the board

definitions.meaning: first meaning: ... a letter, putting it in the postbox
second meaning: ... a notice, putting it up on a noticeboard

explanation.walkthrough: Both senses use the verb: sending by mail and displaying publicly.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both mailing a letter through a pillar box and pinning a notice up for display.

clue.text: Shot lengthy film, avoiding Spain

indicators.note: the film avoids Spain's letter, so it is left out

parts.note: an epic is a long film on a grand scale

explanation.surface: A director films a long movie without going to Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: A pic is short for picture, a photograph or shot.

clue.text: Hairstyle, one captivating husband

indicators.note: captivating holds something captive, so the husband letter is held inside

parts.note: single means one

explanation.surface: A woman whose haircut wins her a husband.
explanation.definitionFit: A shingle is a short bob haircut tapered at the nape, popular in the 1920s.

clue.text: Made to relax in chairs nurses died

indicators.note: to nurse is to hold close, so the died letter is held inside

parts.note: people in chairs are seated

explanation.surface: A grim scene of patients in chairs dying in nurses' care.
explanation.walkthrough: Nurses looks like a plural noun; it is a verb meaning holds.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedated means calmed by a drug, made to relax.

clue.text: Start eating using a finger: shortly, any number

indicators.note: said shortly, the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a digit is a finger
N stands for an unspecified number in maths

explanation.surface: Someone is told to tuck in with their fingers without fuss.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb is an informal invitation to begin a meal, as in telling guests to tuck in.

clue.text: Expecting to be accompanied by Lee?

parts.note: with means in the company of
Lee Child is the thriller writer who created Jack Reacher; the question mark flags the name

explanation.surface: A query whether someone hopes for Lee's company.
explanation.walkthrough: Lee looks like a person to keep company with; the setter wants the surname of the author Lee Child.
explanation.definitionFit: Being pregnant is described as expecting, so the phrase is an old-fashioned synonym.

clue.text: Second in command at sea briefly returns for a little scrap that brings a charge

definitions.text: a little scrap that brings a charge

indicators.note: a returning word comes back, so the abbreviation is read backwards

parts.words: Second in command at sea briefly
parts.note: Number One is naval slang for the first lieutenant, the second in command of a ship; briefly it is No 1, written NO I

explanation.surface: A naval deputy coming home with a tiny keepsake that costs a fee.
explanation.walkthrough: The digit 1 is read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: An ion is an atom or molecule carrying an electric charge, a tiny particle.

clue.text: Rage at answer to this clue, then have penny-drop moment

parts.note: to seethe is to rage inwardly
every grid entry is a light, so this clue's answer is a light

explanation.surface: A solver fumes at an answer, then suddenly understands it.
explanation.walkthrough: In crossword jargon each answer in the grid is called a light.
explanation.definitionFit: To see the light is an idiom for finally understanding, the moment when the penny drops.

clue.text: Satellite town yet to be built

definitions.text: Satellite town yet to be built

parts.words: Satellite town yet to be built
parts.note: a satellite town is a commuter settlement; here it is a settlement on the Moon, our satellite, not yet built

explanation.walkthrough: Satellite town suggests a suburb around a big city, but the satellite is the Moon.
explanation.definitionFit: A planned settlement on the Moon is a future town on Earth's natural satellite.

clue.text: Sport which the mob runs

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a racquet game played in a walled court
second meaning: criminal schemes such as extortion operated by gangsters

explanation.walkthrough: The mob sounds like a crowd at a match, but it means organised crime.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a court game played with racquets and illegal enterprises run by gangs.

clue.text: By lake I want to plant special crop

indicators.note: to plant is to set something in, so the letter for special is set inside

parts.note: to want is to need

explanation.surface: A farmer beside a lake wants to sow a particular crop.
explanation.definitionFit: Flax is grown for its seed, which is pressed for oil, so the seed is a farm product.

clue.text: Engineer eats last of canteen pap

indicators.note: the engineer eating something takes it inside

parts.note: a sapper is a military engineer

indicators.note: picks the final letter of the word canteen

parts.note: the final letter of canteen

explanation.surface: A soldier tucks into bland mush in the mess hall.
explanation.walkthrough: Pap looks like soft food to go with the canteen; it is short for paparazzo.
explanation.definitionFit: A pap is a paparazzo, a press photographer, and snapper is slang for a photographer.

clue.text: The boot bag made of this

definitions.meaning: first meaning: getting the boot is being sacked, so dismissal
second meaning: coarse cloth such as hessian from which sacks are made

explanation.walkthrough: The boot sounds like footwear, but it is slang for dismissal.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both dismissal from a job and the rough fabric that sacks are made of.

clue.text: A surgical pioneer is a star

parts.note: Joseph Lister pioneered antiseptic surgery

explanation.surface: A claim that a pioneering surgeon is a star.
explanation.definitionFit: An A-lister is a celebrity of the top rank, a star.

clue.text: Almost relaxed, accepting constant postponement

indicators.note: the shortened word accepts the constant inside it
almost all of the word, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: rested means relaxed
pi is the mathematical constant

explanation.surface: Someone nearly calm, putting up with endless delay.
explanation.definitionFit: A respite is a pause or reprieve, a delay, as with a stay of execution.

clue.text: Flashes extremely smart on dresses

indicators.note: the extremes of the word smart are its first and last letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of smart
robes are long dresses or gowns

explanation.surface: Someone shows off very fashionable outfits.
explanation.definitionFit: Strobes are lamps giving rapid bursts of light, so they are flashes.

clue.text: A way to speak

parts.note: an understated description of a speech impediment, a manner of speaking

explanation.walkthrough: The clue is deliberately bland; the answer is a particular manner of speaking with repeated sounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A stutter is a speech pattern of involuntary repetition, so it is a manner of speaking.

clue.text: Graduate exercising a stir in this job?

definitions.text: Graduate exercising a stir in this job?

parts.note: a BA is a Bachelor of Arts

indicators.note: exercising the letters works them about into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A graduate stuck stirring drinks for a living.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the job: a graduate in a coffee shop stirring cups all day.
explanation.definitionFit: A barista makes coffee in a café, a classic job for a graduate, and stirs drinks.

clue.text: Bargain with tough heartless sort of bomber

parts.note: a steal is a bargain

indicators.note: a heartless word loses its middle, leaving its first and last letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of tough, its middle removed

explanation.surface: A deal struck with a hard, unfeeling type.
explanation.definitionFit: The stealth bomber is an aircraft designed to evade radar.

clue.text: Painting, crouch so air can circulate

indicators.note: air circulating moves around, so these letters move into a new order

explanation.surface: Advice to hunch down so that air can flow around you.
explanation.definitionFit: Chiaroscuro is the painting technique of strong contrast between light and shade, so it names a style of art.

clue.text: Wade's opponent in court sounds dear

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Jane ... of ... v Wade, the US abortion case
second meaning: dear sounds like deer

explanation.walkthrough: The second half works by sound: dear is heard as deer, of which the roe is a species.
explanation.definitionFit: The plaintiff in the landmark Supreme Court case was named Roe, which is also a small European deer.

clue.text: Prohibit indirect moves to control temperature

indicators.note: the shuffled word holds the temperature letter inside it, keeping it in check
the letters of the word indirect move about into a new order

explanation.surface: A ban on indirect actions aimed at regulating heat.
explanation.definitionFit: To interdict is to forbid formally, a legal synonym for prohibit.

clue.text: Shot cut trip short

indicators.note: cut short means the word is trimmed, losing its last letter
with cut, the end of the word is chopped off

parts.note: a ride is a trip or journey

explanation.surface: A shot that cuts a trip short.
explanation.walkthrough: Shot is the adjective in being shot of something, meaning free of it.
explanation.definitionFit: To be shot of something is to be rid of it, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Bird makes car leave the roundabout

indicators.note: the car leaving the word means those letters go

parts.note: a carousel is a merry-go-round, also called a roundabout in Britain

explanation.surface: A driver is told how to exit a traffic roundabout.
explanation.walkthrough: Roundabout suggests the traffic junction; here it is the fairground ride.
explanation.definitionFit: The ousel is an old name for the blackbird, and the ring ousel is a thrush.

clue.text: Look embarrassed, like an unsuccessful matador

definitions.meaning: second meaning: pierced by the bull's horns

explanation.walkthrough: Split as two words it is blushing; as one it is what a bull does to a failed bullfighter.
explanation.definitionFit: Blushing is going red, and a bullfighter who fails may be wounded by horns, that is gored.

clue.text: Result of seeing red in Aquae Sulis?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a player shown a red card is sent off for an ...
second meaning: Aquae Sulis was the Roman name for the city of Bath, so it is Bath in its early days

explanation.walkthrough: Seeing red sounds like losing your temper; it is a red card in football or rugby. Bath is the English spa city.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking an early bath is the idiom for being sent off the pitch before the final whistle.
